shorts.title: What you will learn: Sorting: bubble and selection
shorts.script: Watch five bars sort themselves. Today we sort. You will watch bars move, and then you will write the code that moves them. Sorting puts items in order. Bubble sort compares two neighbours, and swaps them if they are in the wrong order. After each pass, the biggest item has moved to the end. Selection sort finds the smallest item, and puts it first. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: What you will learn: Sorting: bubble and selection.

shorts.title: Sorting: bubble and selection in one minute
shorts.script: Sorting puts items in order. Bubble sort compares two neighbours, and swaps them if they are in the wrong order. After each pass, the biggest item has moved to the end. Selection sort finds the smallest item, and puts it first. Think of students who line up by height. Neighbours swap places until the line is right. Each pass moves the biggest unsorted item to its place at the end. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Sorting: bubble and selection in one minute.

shorts.title: Inside the second program
shorts.hook: M holds the index of the smallest item that we
shorts.script: M holds the index of the smallest item that we know so far. The inner loop looks at all the items to the right. A smaller item becomes the new m. After the inner loop, we swap the smallest item into position i. Selection sort makes at most one swap for each pass. The program prints one, three, four, five, eight. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Inside the second program.

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: A swap that loses a value
shorts.hook: Can you spot the bug in sorting, bubble and selection?
shorts.script: Can you spot the bug in sorting, bubble and selection? Bug of the Day. The array is three, one, two. The sorted output has repeated numbers. The swap has no helper box. The first line overwrites a j. The second line copies the same value back. Both boxes now hold one. Save the old value in a helper box first. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Bug of the Day: A swap that loses a value.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: Can you count the swaps in sorting, bubble and selection?
shorts.script: Can you count the swaps in sorting, bubble and selection? Bubble sort is a patient algorithm. It takes many passes, and it never complains. Add a counter to bubble sort. Print how many swaps it made for the array five, three, eight, one, four. Write your answer in the comments. Bubble sort swaps neighbours that are out of order. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Pun and challenge.
